description: Blocks STARTING a heavy operation (VS Code extension rebuild/`vsce package`, a multi-model `review diff`/`quorum`/`brainstorm`/`just-ask` pass, a build/test-suite run, or a GPU model load: stt, whisper-cli, whisper-server, llama-cli, llama-server, mlx_lm/mlx_whisper, or any command handed a .bin/.gguf/.ggml/.safetensors model file) while the machine is short of memory. Two signals, either one blocks: (1) macOS `sysctl kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level` >= RIG_HEAVY_OP_BLOCK_AT_LEVEL (default 2; 1=normal/2=warn/4=critical; Linux PSI fallback); (2) the memory jetsam cannot see, from `vm_stat` (macOS) or /proc/meminfo (Linux): wired share of RAM above RIG_HEAVY_OP_MAX_WIRED_PCT (default 75) or free + inactive + speculative + purgeable below RIG_HEAVY_OP_MIN_AVAILABLE_MB (default 512). Added after 2026-08-27/28 (concurrent heavy agent work drove free memory to ~65MB and hung VS Code windows) and 2026-09-29 (13 concurrent whisper-cli runs wired 95.7% of a 24GB Mac into GPU buffers at NORMAL jetsam pressure and kernel-panicked it). A GPU model load is also refused at once while every slot of the machine-wide GPU slot pool (lib/agenttools_gpu_slots: flock lock files, RIG_GPU_SLOTS default 2, freed by the kernel when a holder dies) is taken; the same load queued through `python3 <agent-tools>/lib/agenttools_gpu_slots run -- <cmd>` is not refused, since that wrapper waits for a slot itself. The hook never waits and keeps no state of its own: it re-reads memory and probes the kernel-managed slot locks on every call, so nothing can leak or deadlock and a retry after memory or a slot frees up passes. No self-bypass and no Telegram hatch-escalation (an objective, self-resolving fact, not a human judgment call); applies to the orchestrator and subagents alike. Fails open when no memory signal is readable and skips only the slot check when the slot lib is missing: an availability circuit-breaker, not a security boundary. on_error=open.
